title: Noisy Air Purifier Requires Expensive Replacement Filters
text:
Noisy Air Purifier Requires Expensive Replacement Filters. In my bedroom, this MOLEKULE MINI AIR PURIFIER (with PECO Purification Technology, White) doesn’t seem to be as effective as my [[ASIN:B01LCX9QWG GermGuardian Air Purifier]] at clearing particulate matter from the air. The Molekule is supposed to destroy (not simply kill) germs, which is why I purchased it (from the manufacturer’s web site). However, there is no way to verify this germ-destroying claim.

My [[ASIN:B07JF53NRK Temtop indoor air quality monitor]] shows about the same readings for particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, and air quality, regardless of which air purifier (Molekule Mini or GermGuardian) that I use. The GermGuardian does come with a UV light for killing germs, and the light does seem to make a difference in how clean the air feels. (Again, there’s no way to verify the manufacturer’s germ-killing claim). The GG UV light requires replacement from time to time, but not as frequently as the manufacturer suggests.

The Molekule Mini is more expensive than the GermGuardian, and much noisier. I find that the Level 3 fan setting (out of 5) is the highest “always on” fan setting that is reasonable, and even this setting makes it hard for a nearby Amazon Echo device to hear the wake word.

The Molekule Mini requires expensive replacement filters every 6 months. The GermGuardian also requires replacement filters, but they’re less expensive, and the GG is pretty forgiving if you don’t replace the filters right away.

The Molekule Mini is kind of heavy, and has a surprisingly large footprint on my bedside table. Unlike the GermGuardian, the Mini lacks a display that shows the particulate matter count, and it doesn’t have an Auto setting that makes the fan speed up automatically if extra pollutants are present in the air. (There is a new, more expensive model of the Molekule Mini that does have some kind of particulate matter display.)

Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the Molekule Mini. After using it for 6 months, I decided to take it out of service. It doesn’t improve the air quality in my bedroom (over what I get with the GermGuardian); it’s too noisy; and the filters are too expensive.

description: Molekule has reimagined the future of clean air through its breakthrough, patented PECO technology that destroys pollutants.
Below are the steps for this process:
Make sure the device is plugged into a working outlet.
Remove the plastic wrap on the PECO-Filter.
Turn the lid clockwise until it fully clicks into place.
Make sure your device is on a flat surface
Try placing the device on floor in between your feet while turning the lid.
You may need to remove the lid and try closing the lid several times until it finally locks into place.
If your device still will not power on follow these steps:
Place your finger on the center button on the lid
Plug the device back in, continue to hold finger on button for 5 seconds
